articles.title: Compute Scarcity Is Permanent. Build a Ladder
articles.summary: Processors are currently scarce because of the same bottleneck: the high-bandwidth memory and the advanced packaging that binds it to the die are capacity-limited across the entire industry. This can't be fixed with a bigger cloud budget or a patient retry loop. This constraint isn't clearing anytime soon and is likely a permanent condition. Businesses need to build for this reality rather than waiting for the shortage to end.

articles.title: The rise of the 1-person growth engineer
articles.summary: No industry leader has created a program or certification for AI fluency yet. It's difficult for individuals and hiring managers to understand whether they're doing cutting-edge work or are part of the status quo. Building a portfolio of proof is really important at this stage. Do the work in public, talk about what you're building, and collect third-party proof and outcomes wherever you can get them.

articles.title: 99% of My Website Traffic Is Bots
articles.summary: PatronView is a donor-research database with 1.5 million profile pages built from public records. In one week, its server served 1.28 million pages while analytics counted only 5,977 pageviews. That is 214 invisible loads for every visible one. Claude-SearchBot crawled 35,000 pages for every visitor it sent back. Amazon crawled 117,000 pages a day and sent none. Cloudflare's bot detector added 2.875 seconds and cut mobile Lighthouse to 58. Removing it restored 99, then an Azure scraper pulled 23,000 pages in an hour. The founder now judges crawlers by pages taken per visitor returned.

articles.title: Inside an Applied AI company
articles.summary: Applied AI companies sell completed work, making the harness, not the model, the core product: tools, integrations, persistence, orchestration, oversight, and evals close the gap from 70% to 98%+ accuracy. Durable advantage comes from compounding knowledge, hardening, and evaluation loops.

articles.title: How to keep thinking
articles.summary: One engineer now runs six or seven AI-agent sessions on the same coding task. Some explore, others build competing versions, and more review and test. Things got faster, but his job slowly became skimming and judging answers instead of forming his own. So he added one deliberately slow habit. He reads dense nonfiction and writes about it without an LLM. As more research, code, and analysis move into agent queues, keep one place where you still have to start with a blank page and decide what you think.

articles.title: Google Launches Gemini 3.7 Flash With a 50% Price Cut Through December
articles.summary: Google has released Gemini 3.7 Flash, three weeks after Gemini 3.6 Flash. Until December 31, API rates are $0.75 per million input tokens and $3.75 per million output tokens. The rates double on January 1. The offer gives developers a defined testing window.

articles.title: ChatGPT Ads Get Automated Bidding, Placements, and URL Parameters
articles.summary: OpenAI has added three new features to its ads platform. The platform will now automatically adjust bids to get the most results from advertisers' budgets. A new Eligible Platforms dropdown allows advertisers to individually deselect ad platforms. There are now new ways to include URL parameters for third-party tracking.

articles.title: ChatGPT for Mac adds opt-in Computer History feature, replacing Chronicle
articles.summary: ChatGPT's new Computer History feature creates a searchable timeline from activity across selected apps and websites. The feature is off by default and must be enabled by each user. Computer History replaces the Chronicle research preview. While Chronicle relied on screenshots, Computer History records interaction events exposed through macOS accessibility features.

articles.title: Land a ‘Buffalo' to Establish a New Market
articles.summary: A sales consultant advised a portfolio company with a greenfield market to focus on one vertical and target large enterprises. The strategy involves attending conferences, creating vertical-specific content, and landing key industry leaders as references. Once established, the company should expand into related verticals to leverage their initial success.

articles.title: The moat paradox
articles.summary: Building a business moat involves solving the hardest core problems, not just relying on Helmer's seven lagging indicators. The leading indicator for a defensible business is solving high-effort, high-risk problems directly tied to core user value. Fear of uncertainty often deters entrepreneurs, but confronting difficult problems can create a sustainable competitive advantage.

articles.title: The Car Got Better. The Deal Got Worse.
articles.summary: US automakers made cars safer and longer-lived, while like-for-like prices fell roughly 45% after inflation.
